llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于生物墨水和肌肉组织工程，未涉及人工智能集成。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML integration in bioprinting workflow; purely biomaterial and tissue engineering study without any machine learning methodology.

summary_zh.motivation: 为修复体积性肌肉损失，工程化3D骨骼肌组织。
summary_zh.method: 开发快速应力松弛生物墨水，打印各向异性支架。
summary_zh.result: 支架促进肌肉再生和功能恢复。
summary_zh.validation: 在大鼠体积性肌肉损失模型中验证。

summary_en.motivation: To engineer 3D skeletal muscle and repair volumetric muscle loss using bioprinted scaffolds.
summary_en.method: A fast stress relaxation bioink was developed to print anisotropic scaffolds with aligned microstructures.
summary_en.result: The bioprinted scaffolds promoted muscle regeneration and functional recovery in a rat VML model.
summary_en.validation: In vivo validation was performed using a rat model of volumetric muscle loss.

papers.title: A Three-Dimensional Bioprinted Copolymer Scaffold with Biocompatibility and Structural Integrity for Potential Tissue Regeneration Applications
papers.abstract: The present study was to investigate the rheological property, printability, and cell viability of alginate−gelatin composed hydrogels as a potential cell-laden bioink for three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting applications. The 2 g of sodium alginate dissolved in 50 mL of phosphate buffered saline solution was mixed with different concentrations (1% (0.5 g), 2% (1 g), 3% (1.5 g), and 4% (2 g)) of gelatin, denoted as GBH-1, GBH-2, GBH-3, and GBH-4, respectively. The properties of the investigated hydrogels were characterized by contact angle goniometer, rheometer, and bioprinter. In addition, the hydrogel with a proper concentration was adopted as a cell-laden bioink to conduct cell viability testing (before and after bioprinting) using Live/Dead assay and immunofluorescence staining with a human corneal fibroblast cell line. The analytical results indicated that the GBH-2 hydrogel exhibited the lowest loss rate of contact angle (28%) and similar rheological performance as compared with other investigated hydrogels and the control group. Printability results also showed that the average wire diameter of the GBH-2 bioink (0.84 ± 0.02 mm (*** p < 0.001)) post-printing was similar to that of the control group (0.79 ± 0.05 mm). Moreover, a cell scaffold could be fabricated from the GBH-2 bioink and retained its shape integrity for 24 h post-printing. For bioprinting evaluation, it demonstrated that the GBH-2 bioink possessed well viability (>70%) of the human corneal fibroblast cell after seven days of printing under an ideal printing parameter combination (0.4 mm of inner diameter needle, 0.8 bar of printing pressure, and 25 °C of printing temperature). Therefore, the present study suggests that the GBH-2 hydrogel could be developed as a potential cell-laden bioink to print a cell scaffold with biocompatibility and structural integrity for soft tissues such as skin, cornea, nerve, and blood vessel regeneration applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了海藻酸钠-明胶生物墨水的流变性和打印性，但未涉及任何AI或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on bioink formulation and printability characterization without any AI integration, machine learning, or autonomous decision-making, which is the core of the AI for Bioprinting direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索藻酸盐-明胶水凝胶作为3D生物打印生物墨水的可行性。
summary_zh.method: 配制不同浓度的凝胶并测试其流变学、可打印性和细胞活性。
summary_zh.result: GBH-2配方(2%明胶)表现出最优的综合性能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过活/死染色和免疫荧光进行细胞活性验证。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate alginate-gelatin hydrogels as potential bioinks for 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Hydrogels with varying gelatin concentrations were characterized for rheology, printability, and cell viability using human corneal fibroblasts.
summary_en.result: The GBH-2 formulation (2% gelatin) showed the best balance of shape integrity and cell viability (>70%) after 7 days.
summary_en.validation: Cell viability was assessed via Live/Dead assay and immunofluorescence staining.
